Thank you, Rahul. Good day, everyone. I'll begin by highlighting a few key takeaways from my 
investor presentation, and Ajay, our CFO, will then walk you through the financials. 
 
STL is a global leader in Digital Connectivity Infrastructure, serving data centers, telcos, citizen 
networks and large enterprises. Our optical connectivity portfolio spans fiber-to-fiber cables, 
speciality cables, connectivity solutions. We are also India's number 1 end-to-end optical 
manufacturer with about 9% global optical fiber cable market share outside China. With 35-plus 
years of leadership and more than 805 global patents filed and granted and 10-plus advanced 
manufacturing facilities with 0 waste to landfill and 0 liquid discharge, STL is leading the next 
wave of the global digital infrastructure buildup. 
 
We're amongst the few companies in the world with presence across the value chain from Glass 
to Gigabit, starting with the purest grade of Silicon, which we transform through advanced 
processes, like silicon tetrachloride formation, chemical vapor deposition and high-precision 
sintering, we create ultra pure glass preforms, which is the backbone of optical fiber. 
 
From there, we draw the highest grade fiber, design high-density cables and develop reliable 
connectivity products that power data centers and telecom networks worldwide. This full stack

This deep integration also gives one of the most complete portfolios across the industry from 
specialty and next-generation fibers to high-density cables to plug-and-play connectivity for 
fiber-to-the-home and AI data center architecture. 
 
Back in September, we laid out Lakshya, our growth road map for FY '29 with the ambition of 
becoming the top 5 global connectivity players and reach INR20,000 crores in revenue. In FY 
'27, the first year of Lakshya, we are putting this plan into motion across 5 clear execution 
priorities. 
 
On the market side, we are actively shifting our revenue mix towards high value-added 
integrated connectivity solutions, are rapidly scaling our footprint in data center segment. To 
maintain our product edge, we are committing 2% of our annual revenue into R&D for next-
generation optical platforms. At the same time, we are driving margin expansion by staying 
relentlessly focused on cost efficiencies and delivering stronger value to our customers. 
 
Finally, to power this entire growth cycle, we're expanding our preform fiber and cable capacities 
by 50% and building a new greenfield facility for pre-term related-solutions. All of this is backed 
by an annual capex commitment of around INR1,000 crores per year through FY '29. As you all 
know, currently, we are at the intersection of 3 powerful multi-year investment cycles, data 
centers, 5G and 6G networks and fiber to the x. 
 
Over the last few quarters, each of these cycles has only become stronger. Data center remains 
the fastest-growing driver for optical fiber demand. CRU recently upgraded its 2026 demand 
projections for this segment to 89% year-on-year, up sharply from 63% last quarter. This is 
underscored by acceleration of investments for hyperscalers and neo clouds. With Morgan 
Stanley revising its 2026 forecast upward from $805 billion to $978 billion and projecting a $1.5 
trillion of investment in 2027. 
 
Our mobile networks, 5G adoption continues to scale rapidly with global 5G subscriptions 
projected to reach 6.4 billion by 2031, and India alone accounting of 1 billion in the same time 
frame. On top of this 5G expansion, global 6G subscriptions are forecast to cross 180 million by 
the end of 2031. 
 
Looking at FTTx deployment -- looking at FTTx deployments accelerating worldwide, 
expanding from 157 million fiber kilometers in 2025 to roughly 166 million fiber kilometers by 
2030. In the U.S. alone, more than 140 million new homes will be connected with fiber by 2030, 
backed by massive government initiatives like BEAD in the U.S. and BharatNet in India. 
Together, these 3 converging cycles create a structured long-term demand tailwind for optical 
fiber and connectivity positioning STL right at the center of the world's next digital infrastructure 
build-out. 
 
Moving on. Slide 10 delves into how the AI revolution and rapid data center expansion are 
creating a once-in-a-generation opportunity for optical connectivity. Global data center capacity

is expected to grow from about 82 gigawatts to about 219 gigawatts by 2030, with over 70% of 
the total demand coming from AI-specific infrastructure. 
 
AI is driving a fundamental step change in fiber intensity across 3 core dimensions: First, is 
scale-out, which appears between the racks. Fiber per switch rack skyrocketed from 500 fibers 
in the cloud era to 12,000 in today's 72 GPU AI nodes, heading towards 16,000 fibers in the 
upcoming architectures. 
 
Next is scale across, which connects multiple AI clusters, buildings and data centers so they can 
operate as one unified AI infrastructure. Every new site multiplies interconnects, 2 data centers 
need 1 link, but 6 data centers need as many as 15 or more. 
 
And finally, scale up, which takes place at the GPU rack level. As speed transitions from 400 
gig to 800 gig and almost to 1.6 terabit, copper hits its physical performance limits and making 
non -- making optical fiber simply non-negotiable. Together, these 3 dynamics present a 
structural step change in fiber intensity. 
 
With our Neuralis end-to-end AI-DC portfolio, STL is uniquely positioned to capture multiyear 
structural growth opportunity across the stack. 
 
Looking at Slide 11, let's look at India's infrastructure landscape, which is rapidly emerging as 
one of our most compelling long-term structural tailwinds. Looking at the capacity rollout, 
India's live DC capacity has reached approximately 1.8 gigawatts, following a record 258-
megawatt additions in the first half of FY '27 alone. 
 
Over the next years, this installed capacity is set to increase nearly sixfold to almost 10.5 
gigawatts by 2031. What makes this investment cycle particularly powerful is the breadth of 
commitment across the board. Hyperscalers like Google, Meta, Microsoft, Amazon are 
deploying tens of billions of dollars. On the other side, we have Indian conglomerates like Tata, 
Adani and Reliance laying out massive long-term capacity plans as well. 
 
Over the last few quarters itself, we've seen massive new announcements coming from Meta and 
Reliance pushing forward with almost 3 gigawatts of development plans to Australia-based 
AirTrunk, which is committing almost $30 billion across Maharashtra and Andhra Pradesh, for 
overall 5 gigawatts of data center capacities. 
 
Adding to this momentum, are landmark commitments like Adani talking about over $100 
billion to build out 5 gigawatts of green AI data centers by 2035. This includes AdaniConneX 
partnering with CoreWeave to build a 240-megawatt campus in Navi Mumbai, which are 
powered by NVIDIA's Vera Rubin platform. Overall, a supportive policy environment with state 
incentives such as stamp duty waivers and 10 to 20 year electricity-duty exemptions, power 
availability and very importantly, the tax holidays extending into 2047. This further de-risking 
and accelerating this data center build out. 
 
Every dollar of the data center capex has a direct multiplier on fiber intensity across DCI, Metro 
and long-haul networks.

performance clearly demonstrates our strategic pivot towards selling higher value-added 
integrated solutions than stand-alone products which is gaining strong traction in the market.

100% factory-tested and arrives ready to install with the latest high-density connector 
technology.

faster deployment and massive GPU clustering. It reduces deployment complexity and 
accelerates time to service. Supported by local manufacturing in South Carolina, this launch 
strengthens our position with the U.S. hyperscaler and neocloud providers.

Firstly, our G.654.E fiber is now fully commercialized and delivers 30% lower signal loss.

ultra-low-latency infrastructure required for tomorrow's AI workloads.

growth of 145% year-on-year basis and 32% quarter-on-quarter basis. On an H1 basis, revenue 
grew to INR4,439 crores, up 116% compared to H1 FY '26.

high-value optical connectivity.

INR14 crores in H1 FY '26, reflecting the strong operating leverage in our business. In summary, 
these results demonstrate strong revenue momentum, expanding margins and bottom line 
execution, setting us up remarkably well for the remainder of FY '27.

North America remains our key growth engines driven by hyperscaler demand, our presence
